summary.motive: Storm both C-gaps with the stacked backers while the ends slant inward, so the protection must choose an edge while the anchoring nose erases any interior answer.
summary.keyDefender: JACK — the weak stack backer whose outside burst arrives exactly after the tackle chases the slanting end inside
summary.whyItWorks: The four-man weave scrambles every slide call, the back can only take one storming edge, and man coverage behind removes all hot answers while the nose makes climbing the pocket impossible.
summary.failureMode: Rhythm throws released before the weave develops, or max protect with two backs — the dog needs a standard five-man protection count to manufacture its free runner.

beats.title: 1. Stacks Hide the Storm
beats.text: Nothing about the pre-snap picture says blitz: three linemen across, three backers hidden directly behind them at identical depth, one safety high. Four potential rushers are invisible inside that single file.

beats.title: 2. Ends Slant In, Edges Storm Out
beats.text: The call fires as a four-man weave: both ends dart inside to the B-gaps while Jack and Spur burst outward through the C-gaps their linemen just vacated. Every blocker’s first target is already moving the wrong way.

beats.title: 3. The Nose Anchors While Protection Tilts
beats.text: The nose swallows the guard-center combo and refuses both A-gaps, so nobody can slide to help. The running back commits to the strong stormer — which means the weak edge now belongs to nobody.

beats.title: 4. Free Edge Off the Blind Side
beats.text: The tackle chased the slanting end inside and the left edge stands empty. Jack rounds it untouched and buries the quarterback as he climbs — the price of blocking rules written against a static front.

relations.tell: Pre-snap it reads like plain Cover 3 stack — no walk-ups anywhere; every rusher hid directly behind a lineman until the snap.
